headlines.headline: The overnight futures recovery is holding but cooling into the 5 AM PT hour: SPY ETF +0.74% premarket at 7:55 AM ET, easing from the ~1.1% S&P futures reading earlier in the morning, with 281 stocks up vs 135 down across 421 premarket prints.
headlines.why_it_matters: The V-shape off the overnight lows (Nasdaq-100 futures -2.4%, S&P -1.4%) is intact, but the fade from the morning highs shows buyers are not chasing into the open.

headlines.headline: CVS Health beat big before the open: Q3 revenue $108.4B (+5.4% year over year) vs ~$104.7B expected, adjusted EPS $2.09 vs ~$1.65 expected, and it raised full-year guidance — adjusted EPS to at least $8.20 (from $7.90-$8.10) and operating cash flow to at least $15.5B (from at least $11.5B).
headlines.why_it_matters: A beat plus a raise is a sentiment tailwind for health care, already the premarket's strongest group (+1.99%) — it validates the post-sweep health-care rotation rather than just riding it.

headlines.headline: Uber's Q4 profit guide disappointed: Q4 non-GAAP EPS guided to $0.95-$0.99 vs $1.06 expected, even as Q3 revenue of $14.77B (+10%, slowest since Q1 2021) topped the $14.69B estimate; Reuters cites driver shortages, higher fuel costs and the Middle East conflict (a 75bp drag on Q3 Mobility bookings growth, 100bp assumed for Q4). Uber also targets ~700 fully driverless vehicles by year-end and 2,000+ by end-2027.
headlines.why_it_matters: Guidance, not the quarter, sets the tone here — a soft profit outlook outweighs a revenue beat for a stock already down on consumer-demand worries.

headlines.headline: McDonald's split the print: Q3 EPS $3.57 vs $3.38 expected, but revenue $7.16B vs $7.28B expected — an EPS beat with a revenue miss.
headlines.why_it_matters: Mixed read on the consumer: profitability held while top-line softness keeps the demand question open into the ISM services data at 10 AM ET.

headlines.headline: Amazon is the premarket's biggest single lift: up about 3.45% premarket, contributing about 0.13 points of the market's move, with Apple and Microsoft each adding about 0.09 points; no fresh Amazon-specific headline accompanied the move in this hour's sourced pages.
headlines.why_it_matters: A megacap this large moving ~3.5% does index-level work on its own — it is a large share of why the SPY premarket gain is holding despite chip weakness.

headlines.headline: Fresh analyst split on Apple today (MarketBeat ratings tracker): DZ Bank downgraded Apple to Sell (from Hold) with a $300 target, while Goldman Sachs set a $380 target — a wide disagreement landing the day after Apple's December-quarter margin guide (45-46% vs 47.9% in September) pressured the stock.
headlines.why_it_matters: Conflicting analyst calls on the same morning usually widen the intraday range rather than set direction — Apple is a tug-of-war name into the open.

headlines.headline: Carried: Musk-linked names remain the premarket's biggest drags — SpaceX and Tesla were the largest drags on the premarket map (-0.20 and -0.12 points respectively), extending Tuesday's political repricing after Democrats' sweep; Reuters earlier put both down around 4% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: The political discount on Musk-linked names is persisting while the broader market recovers — it is a stock-specific overhang, not broad risk-off.

headlines.headline: New political detail for the data-center trade: Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the Texas governorship after campaigning for a moratorium on new data centers until stronger resident protections are set, and Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms won in Georgia, another major data-center market — adding a state-level constraint to the AI buildout story alongside memory, packaging and power shortages.
headlines.why_it_matters: It turns the vague 'tougher AI oversight' fear into a concrete state-level mechanism — permitting risk for data centers, which is why data-center operators and chips are lagging the recovery.

headlines.headline: Carried: AMD's beat still anchors the AI tape — Q3 revenue $13.38B (+45%) vs $13.09B expected, adjusted EPS $2.09 vs $1.95, data-center revenue +97% to $8.55B, Q4 guided to ~$17B vs $16.2B expected, with 2027 growth above 80% flagged; Reuters put AMD up 6.2% premarket, Nvidia up 0.5%, though chips/memory as a group were -1.79% premarket at 7:55 AM ET.
headlines.why_it_matters: The single-stock AI strength is real, but the group-level chip weakness shows the election overhang is offsetting it — stock-picking, not sector beta, is driving chips this morning.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news in the last hour; carrying the Q3 story: revenue $357.2M (+43% year over year, vs ~$348.32M consensus), record Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF coverage 1.67x, EPS $0.33 in line, distribution held at $0.525, with full-year guidance tightened on the Nov 3 call to Adjusted EBITDA $770-780M and DCF $495-505M. Next dated item: the $0.525 distribution pays Friday Nov 6.

After the close today: Qualcomm and Arm earnings.
Whether the premarket fade (SPY +0.74% at 7:55 AM ET vs ~1.1% earlier) stabilizes or extends into the 6:30 AM PT open.
First policy signals from incoming Democratic congressional leadership on AI/data-center oversight and clean-energy spending.
Fri Nov 6: October nonfarm payrolls; USAC's $0.525 distribution pays.
analysis: What changed versus the 4:00 AM brief: the story shifted from the election repricing itself to this morning's earnings slate landing on top of it. CVS's beat-and-raise is the cleanest new positive — it validates the health-care rotation rather than just riding it — while Uber's soft Q4 profit guide and McDonald's revenue miss are the counterweight, keeping the consumer read mixed into the ISM services print. The futures tape is the tell: the overnight V-shape held, but SPY's premarket gain faded from ~1.1% to +0.74% by 7:55 AM ET, and breadth (281 up/135 down) is positive but not euphoric. The Texas/Georgia governor detail sharpens the data-center story from vague oversight fear into concrete permitting risk, which helps explain why chips as a group (-1.79%) lag even as AMD (+6.2% premarket) shines. Signal vs noise: CVS's raise, Uber's guide cut and the state-level data-center constraint are signal; the single-outlet report of a CVS split into two companies is unconfirmed noise for now — it does not appear in CVS's own earnings release, so it is excluded from the headlines above. The Nasdaq-100 remains in correction, so today's recovery is a bounce inside a damaged tape, not a trend change.
